title: SAT Grammar: Punctuation
subtitle: 23 punctuation skills · 2 examples and 5 SAT questions per skill

sections.title: Sentence Boundaries: Periods, Run-ons, Comma Splices, and Fragments
sections.explanation_en: An independent clause has a subject, a verb, and a complete idea; it can stand alone as a sentence. When two independent clauses meet, you must separate them correctly—usually with a period. A comma alone between two independent clauses is a comma splice, and no punctuation is a run-on. Never use a period to cut off a phrase or a dependent clause (that makes a fragment). Watch out: the second clause often begins with a phrase ("With a pressure cooker, …", "Built into the rocks, …") that hides its subject.
sections.explanation_zh: 獨立子句有主詞、動詞，意思完整，可以單獨成為一個句子。兩個獨立子句相接時，必須正確分開，最常用句號。兩個獨立子句之間只用逗號連接，叫做「逗號拼接」(comma splice)，是錯誤的；完全沒有標點叫做「連寫句」(run-on)，也是錯誤的。不可以用句號把片語或從屬子句單獨切開，否則會變成「句子片段」(fragment)。注意：第二個子句常以片語開頭（例如 With a pressure cooker, …），要找出它真正的主詞與動詞。
examples: Jamaican British artist Willard Wigan is known for his remarkable microsculptures. Creations so small that they are best viewed through a microscope, Wigan’s sculptures are made from tiny natural materials, such as spiderweb strands. [Digital SAT 6, Module 1, Q24]

What increases is the rate at which the water turns to vapor. With a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps the vapor in the pot, creating pressure that allows the temperature of the water to increase past its boiling point. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q24]

questions.passage: The intense pressure found in the deep ocean can affect the structure of proteins in fish’s cells, distorting the proteins’ shape. The chemical trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) counters this effect, ensuring that proteins retain their original ______ is found in high concentrations in the cells of the deepest-dwelling fish.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses ("The chemical TMAO counters..." and "TMAO is found...") must be separated. A period does this correctly. B is a run-on, C a comma splice, and D joins them with "and" but no comma and creates confusion with "configurations and TMAO" as a compound object.

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q22 — also SAT 8 M2 Q21
questions.passage: After the United Kingdom began rolling out taxes equivalent to a few cents on single-use plastic grocery bags in 2011, plastic-bag consumption decreased by up to ninety ______ taxes are subject to what economists call the “rebound effect”: as the change became normalized, plastic-bag use started to creep back up.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses must be separated; a period does this. A is a comma splice, D is a run-on, and B needs a comma before "and."

questions.passage: Hegra is an archaeological site in present-day Saudi Arabia and was the second largest city of the Nabataean Kingdom (fourth century BCE to first century CE). Archaeologist Laila Nehmé recently traveled to Hegra to study its ancient ______ into the rocky outcrops of a vast desert, these burial chambers seem to blend seamlessly with nature.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Built into the rocky outcrops..." introduces the second independent clause ("these burial chambers seem..."). A period separates the two sentences. B–D create a run-on/comma splice or misattach the modifier.

questions.passage: In 2010, archaeologist Noel Hidalgo Tan was visiting the twelfth-century temple of Angkor Wat in Cambodia when he noticed markings of red paint on the temple ______ the help of digital imaging techniques, he discovered the markings to be part of an elaborate mural containing over 200 paintings.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "With the help of digital imaging techniques, he discovered..." is a new independent clause, so a period is needed. A is a comma splice, B a run-on, C illogical.

questions.passage: The first computerized spreadsheet, Dan Bricklin’s VisiCalc, improved financial recordkeeping not only by providing users with an easy means of adjusting data in spreadsheets but also by automatically updating all calculations that were dependent on these ______ to VisiCalc’s release, changing a paper spreadsheet often required redoing the entire sheet by hand, a process that could take days.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Prior to VisiCalc’s release, changing a paper spreadsheet often required..." is a new independent clause, so a period is needed after "adjustments." B is a comma splice; A and D fuse the sentences and make "prior to" illogically modify "adjustments."

sections.title: Comma + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so)
sections.explanation_en: A comma can join two independent clauses—but only when it is followed by one of the seven coordinating conjunctions: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so (FANBOYS). The pattern is IC, but IC. Put the comma before the conjunction, not after it. If the words after and/but have no new subject, you are only joining two verbs, so use no comma ("The archivist catalogued the letters and scanned each page").
sections.explanation_zh: 逗號可以連接兩個獨立子句，但後面必須加上七個對等連接詞之一：for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so（口訣 FANBOYS）。句型是 獨立子句, but 獨立子句.，逗號放在連接詞前面，不是後面。如果 and / but 後面沒有新的主詞，只是連接兩個動詞，就不加逗號（例：The archivist catalogued the letters and scanned each page.）。
examples: The liquid metals in Earth’s core circulate constantly, and this circulation generates electrical currents that flow between Earth’s North and South magnetic poles. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q28]
No one was hurt, but in two hours the original Globe was gone. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q20]

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q21 — also SAT 10 M1 Q21
questions.passage: Typically, underlines, scribbles, and notes left in the margins by a former owner lower a book’s ______ when the former owner is a famous poet like Walt Whitman, such markings, known as marginalia, can be a gold mine to literary scholars.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses with contrasting ideas are joined; a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" is correct. B is a run-on, C a comma splice, D lacks the comma before "but."

questions.passage: Materials scientist Marie-Agathe Charpagne and her colleagues believed they could improve on the multicomponent alloy NiCoCr, an equal-proportions mixture of nickel (Ni), cobalt (Co), and chromium (Cr), by replacing chromium with ruthenium ______ the alloy that resulted, NiCoRu, turned out to be an unsuitable replacement for NiCoCr.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two contrasting independent clauses are joined with a comma plus "but." A is a run-on, B lacks the comma, C is a comma splice.

questions.passage: Many mechanical calculators were powered by a notched cylinder mechanism called the Leibniz wheel. Leibniz wheel calculators were popular in the first half of the twentieth ______ these ingenious devices were eventually replaced by electronic calculators.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses with a contrast are joined with a comma + "but." A is a run-on, B a comma splice, D creates an illogical relative clause.

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 10, Module 1, Q20 — also SAT 1 M2 Q20
questions.passage: The Alvarez theory, developed in 1980 by physicist Luis Walter Alvarez and his geologist son Walter Alvarez, maintained that the secondary effects of an asteroid impact caused many dinosaurs and other animals to die ______ it left unexplored the question of whether unrelated volcanic activity might have also contributed to the mass extinctions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined with a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but." A lacks the comma, C is a run-on, D is a comma splice.

questions.passage: The archivist catalogued the damaged ______ scanned each page at high resolution.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Scanned" shares the subject "the archivist"; there is no second subject, so this is ONE clause with a compound verb. Do not put a comma (or semicolon) before "and" when it joins two verbs.

sections.title: The Semicolon Between Two Independent Clauses
sections.explanation_en: A semicolon works like a "soft period." It joins two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction: IC; IC. Test it exactly like a period: the words on both sides must be able to stand alone as sentences. Never put a semicolon before a phrase or a dependent clause. (A semicolon is not normally used with FANBOYS: write ", but", not "; but".)
sections.explanation_zh: 分號就像「較輕的句號」，用來連接兩個意思密切相關的獨立子句，中間不需要連接詞：獨立子句; 獨立子句. 判斷方法和句號完全一樣：分號左右兩邊都必須能單獨成為完整句子。分號後面不可以接片語或從屬子句。（分號通常不和 FANBOYS 一起用：寫「, but」而不是「; but」。）
examples: Oddly, there is no evidence that any type of bottle gourd is native to the Western Hemisphere; either the fruit or its seeds must have somehow been carried from Asia or Africa. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q18]
Sher-Gil longed to return to her childhood home of India; only there, she believed, could her art truly flourish. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q27]

questions.passage: Seneca sculptor Marie Watt’s blanket art comes in a range of shapes and sizes. In 2004, Watt sewed strips of blankets together to craft a 10-by-13-inch ______ in 2014, she arranged folded blankets into two large stacks and then cast them in bronze, creating two curving 18-foot-tall blue-bronze pillars.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses ("In 2004, Watt sewed..." / "in 2014, she arranged...") are joined without a conjunction, so a semicolon is required. C and D are comma splices; A is a run-on.

questions.passage: Physical materials can be classified by how much light passes through them. Clear glass, which is classified as transparent, allows all (or almost all) light to pass ______ wax paper, which is classified as translucent, allows only some light to pass through.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined with no conjunction, so a semicolon is required. A is a comma splice; B is a run-on; D lacks the needed comma before "and."

questions.passage: That the geographic center of North America lay in the state of North Dakota was conceded by all ______ establishing its precise coordinates proved more divisive.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, so a semicolon is required. B is a comma splice, C a run-on; a colon (A) does not fit because the second clause contrasts rather than explains.

questions.passage: Sociologist Todd Gitlin co-opted the term “recombinant,” normally used in reference to genetic engineering, to describe serialized television shows of the 1980s. Gitlin’s use of the term referenced TV studios’ practice of repackaging successful narrative formulas as new ______ even shows that varied only slightly from other shows still attracted sizeable audiences.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is needed after "content." "In that era" introduces the second clause and is followed by a comma.

questions.passage: Radio astronomers detecting fast radio bursts initially struggled to isolate their stellar ______ subsequent observations using the CHIME telescope confirmed that magnetars were a primary source.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Both sides are independent clauses, so a semicolon works. A is a comma splice, C a run-on, and D puts an unnecessary comma after "and."

sections.title: Conjunctive Adverbs Starting the Second Clause: “; however,” / “. However,”
sections.explanation_en: Words like however, therefore, thus, rather, instead, for example, by contrast, in fact are conjunctive adverbs (transition words), not conjunctions. They cannot join two independent clauses by themselves. When the transition begins the second clause, put a semicolon or period before it and a comma after it: IC; however, IC. or IC. However, IC. Using only commas ("IC, however, IC") creates a comma splice.
sections.explanation_zh: however, therefore, thus, rather, instead, for example, by contrast, in fact 等是「連接副詞」（轉折詞），不是連接詞，不能單獨連接兩個獨立子句。當轉折詞放在第二個子句開頭時，它前面要用分號或句號，後面加逗號：獨立子句; however, 獨立子句. 或 獨立子句. However, 獨立子句. 如果前後都只用逗號（IC, however, IC），就是逗號拼接錯誤。
examples: However, the differences between the 1881 first edition and the 1908 edition of his novel A Portrait of a Lady are extreme, even by James’s standards; in fact, some critics regard the two editions as two different novels altogether. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q29]

Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers. However, according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia, Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q28]

questions.passage: To humans, it does not appear that the golden orb-weaver spider uses camouflage to capture its ______ the brightly colored arachnid seems to wait conspicuously in the center of its large circular web for insects to approach. Researcher Po Peng of the University of Melbourne has explained that the spider’s distinctive coloration may in fact be part of its appeal.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined here. "Rather" is a conjunctive adverb that begins the second clause, so a semicolon goes before it and a comma after it. A is a comma splice; B is a run-on; C puts the semicolon in the wrong place.

questions.passage: Cognitive load theory posits that working memory can process only a limited number of information chunks ______ instructional designers must structure educational software to minimize unnecessary mental effort.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Therefore" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction; it cannot join clauses by itself. Use a semicolon before it and a comma after it. A is a comma splice; C and D are run-ons.

questions.passage: Pine seedlings inoculated with ectomycorrhizal fungi demonstrate enhanced phosphorus ______ uninoculated seedlings in nutrient-poor soils exhibit severely stunted root development.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by the transition "by contrast": semicolon before, comma after. The contrast describes the second clause, so the transition belongs at its start. A is a comma splice; C is a run-on; D attaches "by contrast" to the wrong clause.

questions.passage: Economists evaluating microfinance initiatives observed significant improvements in local ______ during periods of macroeconomic instability, small-business survival rates remained fragile.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "However" introduces a contrast with the second clause. Start a new sentence (or use a semicolon) before it, and put a comma after it. A and D are comma splices; C is a run-on.

questions.passage: The expedition reached the summit two days ahead of ______ the descent took twice as long as planned because of a sudden blizzard.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses; "however" contrasts the second with the first: semicolon before, comma after. B is a comma splice; C is a run-on; D omits the comma after the adverb.

sections.title: Conjunctive Adverbs Ending the First Clause: “, however;” / “, though;”
sections.explanation_en: This is the SAT's favorite hard pattern. Sometimes the transition word belongs to the first clause because it contrasts that clause with the previous sentence. Then it goes at the end of clause 1 with a comma before it, and the semicolon comes after it: IC, however; IC. To decide, ask: Which idea is the adverb contrasting? If clause 2 simply explains or supports clause 1, the adverb belongs to clause 1. The semicolon must always sit exactly at the boundary between the two independent clauses.
sections.explanation_zh: 這是 SAT 最常考的難題型。有時轉折詞屬於第一個子句，因為它是把第一個子句和前一句做對比。這時轉折詞放在第一個子句的結尾，前面加逗號，分號放在它後面：獨立子句, however; 獨立子句. 判斷方法：問自己「這個轉折詞在對比哪兩個想法？」如果第二個子句只是在解釋或支持第一個子句，轉折詞就屬於第一個子句。分號永遠要放在兩個獨立子句的交界處。
examples: Only five of these dances are included in international ballroom dance competitions, however: rumba, samba, cha-cha-cha, paso doble, and jive—the last of which is grouped with the other Latin dances despite not having Latin roots. [Digital SAT 6, Module 2, Q24]
Siderophiles are much more abundant in the mantle than predicted in that model, however. [Digital SAT 10, Module 1, Q30]

questions.passage: Sociologist Alton Okinaka sits on the review board tasked with adding new sites to the Hawai‘i Register of Historic Places, which includes Pi‘ilanihale Heiau and the ‘Ōpaeka‘a Road Bridge. Okinaka doesn’t make such decisions ______ all historical designations must be approved by a group of nine other experts from the fields of architecture, archaeology, history, and Hawaiian culture.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "However" belongs to the first clause (it contrasts with the previous sentence), so it is set off with a comma and followed by a semicolon that separates the two independent clauses. B would link "however" illogically to the second clause.

questions.passage: During the English neoclassical period (1660–1789), many writers imitated the epic poetry and satires of ancient Greece and Rome. They were not the first in England to adopt the literary modes of classical ______ some of the most prominent figures of the earlier Renaissance period were also influenced by ancient Greek and Roman literature.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "However" belongs with the first clause (it contrasts with the previous sentence), and a semicolon separates the two independent clauses. A and B are comma splices; D wrongly attaches "however" to the second clause, where it makes no sense (the second clause supports rather than contrasts with the first).

questions.passage: Chondrites are stony meteorites that are undifferentiated—that is, their contents have not melted and separated into distinct layers. They are hardly ______ many chondrites experience aqueous alteration as a result of exposure to fluids, as well as fracturing, veining, and localized melting due to collisions with other objects.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "They are hardly pristine, though" is a complete clause (with "though" as an adverb at its end). A semicolon then separates it from the next independent clause "many chondrites experience...".

questions.passage: Jetties—long, narrow structures that extend from a landmass into the water—are often constructed to protect coastlines from erosion. Jetties can sometimes have the opposite ______ obstructing the natural flow of sand along the shore can lead to increased erosion in some areas.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Though" is an adverb ending the first clause, set off by a comma. A semicolon then separates the two independent clauses. B and D are comma splices/run-ons; C attaches "though" to the second clause, making it a dependent clause fragment after the semicolon.

questions.passage: With the development of new technologies that use natural resources more efficiently, the overall consumption of those resources might be expected to decrease. Economists have observed that improvements in efficiency often correlate negatively with resource ______ efficiency gains, lowering the cost of use, may increase demand to the extent that resource consumption ultimately rises.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Though" ends the first clause as a contrast adverb (set off with a comma); a semicolon then separates the two independent clauses. A and D create comma splices; B makes the second part a dependent clause after a semicolon.

sections.title: Conjunctive Adverbs Interrupting One Clause: “, however,”
sections.explanation_en: When there is only one independent clause, a transition word like however or though is an interrupter. Set it off with a comma on both sides: Subject, however, verb… A semicolon is wrong here because there is no second independent clause for it to separate—it would split the subject from its verb. Tip: if the words after the transition are only a phrase (e.g., "feeling that…"), there is no clause boundary, so use commas only.
sections.explanation_zh: 當句子裡只有一個獨立子句時，however、though 等轉折詞是插入語，前後都要加逗號：主詞, however, 動詞… 這時不能用分號，因為沒有第二個獨立子句可以分隔；用分號會把主詞和動詞切開。小技巧：如果轉折詞後面只是片語（例如 feeling that…），就沒有子句交界，只用逗號。
examples: Tadpole shrimp (Triops longicaudatus) embryos, for example, can pause development for over ten years during extended periods of drought. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q28]
Larch trees, for instance, lose their needles every fall. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q27]

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q25 — also SAT 9 M1 Q22
questions.passage: Journalists have dubbed Gil Scott-Heron the “godfather of rap,” a title that has appeared in hundreds of articles about him since the 1990s. Scott-Heron himself resisted the godfather ______ feeling that it didn’t encapsulate his devotion to the broader African American blues music tradition as well as “bluesologist,” the moniker he preferred.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "However" interrupts one sentence (the participial phrase "feeling that..." is not an independent clause), so it is set off by a pair of commas. D uses a semicolon, which would require an independent clause after it.

questions.passage: Digital artist Jung (Lulu) Chen primarily uses a suite of software tools to create illustrations for children’s books. To manifest the warm and welcoming atmospheres that are a signature of her ______ she occasionally relies on more traditional art techniques, such as painting with watercolors.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The introductory infinitive phrase ends at "work," and "though" is an interrupting adverb within the same sentence; it needs commas on both sides before the main clause "she occasionally relies...." Semicolons (C, D) would require independent clauses on both sides.

questions.passage: Quantum entanglement links pairs of particles so that measuring one instantly reveals information about the other, even across vast distances. This ______ cannot be used to send messages faster than the speed of light.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Here "however" sits inside a single independent clause ("This phenomenon...cannot be used..."), interrupting subject and verb. An interrupter takes paired commas. B and C put a semicolon between a subject and its verb; D leaves the interrupter unclosed.

questions.passage: Everyone called the young linguist a walking dictionary; he ______ disliked the nickname and asked colleagues to use his name instead.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The semicolon after "dictionary" already separates the two clauses. In the second clause, "however" interrupts the subject ("he himself") and the verb ("disliked"), so it needs a comma on both sides.

questions.passage: Most critics praised the film’s groundbreaking visual effects. Its ______ was widely considered weak and predictable.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: There is only one clause ("Its screenplay…was widely considered weak"), and "however" interrupts its subject and verb, so paired commas are needed. A semicolon (B, D) would split the subject from its verb.

sections.title: “Though”: Adverb (= however) vs. Conjunction (= although)
sections.explanation_en: Though has two jobs. (1) As an adverb meaning however, it is set off by commas: at the end of a sentence ("…far higher than projected, though."), in the middle of a clause ("The novel, though, still raises questions"), or at the end of clause 1 before a semicolon or colon. (2) As a conjunction meaning although, it begins a dependent clause and takes no comma after it ("Though the museum is small, its collection…"). Test: if you can replace it with however, it is an adverb; if you can replace it with although, it is a conjunction.
sections.explanation_zh: though 有兩種用法。(1) 當副詞，意思是「然而」(= however)，要用逗號隔開：可放在句尾（…far higher than projected, though.）、子句中間（The novel, though, still raises questions），或第一個子句的結尾、分號或冒號之前。(2) 當連接詞，意思是「雖然」(= although)，引導從屬子句，後面不加逗號（Though the museum is small, its collection…）。判斷方法：能換成 however → 副詞；能換成 although → 連接詞。
examples: Hopper’s subsequent career would involve more than just equations, though: as a pioneering computer programmer, Hopper would help usher in the digital age. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q22 (adverb)]
Even though bats prefer very sweet nectar, the plants that attract them have evolved to produce nectar that is only moderately sweet. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q19 (conjunction)]

questions.passage: The new bridge was completed in record time. Its construction costs were far higher than originally ______
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A sentence-final "though" (= however) takes a comma before it and the period after it. A semicolon or colon cannot introduce a single adverb.

questions.passage: ______ the museum is small, its collection of Ming dynasty ceramics is considered one of the finest in the world.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Here "though" means "although": it is a conjunction that begins a dependent clause, so no comma follows it. The comma after "small" ends the dependent clause. C creates a comma splice.

questions.passage: The mountain trail is only three kilometers ______ it climbs nearly 900 meters from the parking lot to the summit.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Here "though" = "although" and begins a dependent clause, which is joined to the main clause with a comma. C and D cut the dependent clause off as a fragment; B puts the comma in the wrong place.

questions.passage: Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein was published more than two centuries ago. The ______ still raises urgent questions about scientific responsibility.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Though" (= however) interrupts one independent clause between its subject ("The novel") and verb ("raises"), so it takes a comma on both sides. B and C put a semicolon between subject and verb.

questions.passage: Most residents supported building a new public library. The city council rejected the ______ it cited rising construction costs as its main concern.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Though" contrasts the council's decision with the residents' support (the previous sentence), so it ends the first clause: comma before it, then a semicolon at the clause boundary. B wrongly makes the second clause contrast with the first; C and D are comma splices.

sections.title: The Colon Introducing an Explanation
sections.explanation_en: A colon must come after a complete independent clause. It introduces something that explains, defines, or specifies what the first clause announced. What comes after the colon may be another complete clause. Ask: Could I put "namely" or "that is" here? If yes, and the left side is a full sentence, the colon is correct. Use a semicolon instead when the second clause merely adds or contrasts rather than explains.
sections.explanation_zh: 冒號前面必須是完整的獨立子句。冒號後面的內容用來解釋、定義或具體說明前面子句提到的事情，可以是另一個完整子句。判斷方法：能不能在這裡換成「namely（也就是）」或「that is（即）」？如果可以，而且冒號左邊是完整句子，冒號就是正確的。如果第二個子句只是補充或對比，而不是解釋，就用分號。
examples: A recent study explains why: making sugar is energy-intensive, and it is more advantageous for plants to make a large amount of low-sugar nectar than a small amount of high-sugar nectar. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q19]

Public-awareness campaigns about the need to reduce single-use plastics can be successful, says researcher Kim Borg of Monash University in Australia, when these campaigns give consumers a choice: for example, Japan achieved a 40 percent reduction in plastic-bag use after cashiers were instructed to ask customers whether they wanted a bag. [Digital SAT 10, Module 2, Q18]

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q25 — also SAT 8 M2 Q24
questions.passage: Over twenty years ago, in a landmark experiment in the psychology of choice, professor Sheena Iyengar set up a jam-tasting booth at a grocery store. The number of jams available for tasting ______ some shoppers had twenty-four different options, others only six. Interestingly, the shoppers with fewer jams to choose from purchased more jam.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The second part explains how the number varied, so a colon (which introduces an explanation after an independent clause) is correct. B is a comma splice; C and D create an illogical/garbled structure with "while" followed by another comma-joined clause.

questions.passage: For thousands of years, humans have used domesticated goats (Capra hircus) to clear land of unwanted vegetation. When it comes to their diets, goats are notoriously ______ they will devour all kinds of shrubs and weeds, leaving virtually no part of any plant unconsumed.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The second clause explains what "indiscriminate" means, so a colon (after an independent clause) is correct. B is a comma splice, C a run-on, A lacks a comma before "and."

questions.passage: As cheesemaking practices spread throughout Europe and Asia during and after the Neolithic, divergent strategies for preserving milk ______ whereas rennet-coagulated cheesemaking became key to milk preservation in Europe and Southwest Asia, acid-heat coagulation methods became common among nomadic herding populations of the northeastern Eurasian steppe.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first part is a complete sentence; the second part explains what the "divergent strategies" were. A colon introduces this explanation. D creates a comma splice, A a run-on, B an illogical compound.

questions.passage: Along with carbon dioxide concentration and temperature, light intensity affects the chemical reaction rate of ______ as light intensity increases, so does the rate at which the reactants (water and carbon dioxide) are converted into their products (glucose and oxygen).
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The second independent clause explains how light intensity affects the rate, so a colon is appropriate. B is a comma splice, D a run-on, A lacks the comma before "and."

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 10, Module 2, Q25 — also SAT 1 M1 Q24
questions.passage: Researchers studying magnetosensation have determined why some soil-dwelling roundworms in the Southern Hemisphere move in the opposite direction of Earth’s magnetic field when searching for ______ in the Northern Hemisphere, the magnetic field points down, into the ground, but in the Southern Hemisphere, it points up, toward the surface and away from worms’ food sources.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The second independent clause explains why the worms behave this way, so a colon is appropriate. B is a comma splice, D a run-on, C creates a confusing structure.

sections.title: The Colon Introducing a List or a Specific Item
sections.explanation_en: A colon can also introduce a list, a noun phrase, or even a single word that names what the clause announced ("three goals: …", "the ideal city for a young artist: Paris"). The rule is still the same: the words before the colon must form a complete sentence. A transition word can end that clause before the colon ("…competitions, however: rumba, samba…").
sections.explanation_zh: 冒號也可以引出清單、名詞片語，甚至一個單字，用來說明前面子句所提到的東西（例如 three goals: …、the ideal city for a young artist: Paris）。規則不變：冒號前面必須是完整句子。轉折詞也可以放在冒號前、第一個子句的結尾（…competitions, however: rumba, samba…）。
examples: Amrita Sher-Gil was living in what must have seemed like the ideal city for a young artist: Paris. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q27]
In addition, Zufall suggested selling the product under a child-friendly name: Play-Doh. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q20]

questions.passage: In February 1919, following the end of the First World War, women from ten countries around the world convened the Inter-Allied Women’s Conference in Paris. The conference’s goals were ______ ensure women’s participation in the proceedings of the Paris Peace Conference, to secure the right of women to serve in the League of Nations, and to advocate for human rights.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The conference’s goals were threefold" is complete; a colon introduces the list of the three goals that follows. B and D would leave the list as a fragment; C runs them together.

questions.passage: A study published by Rice University geoscientist Ming Tang in 2019 offers a new explanation for the origin of Earth’s ______ structures called arcs, towering ridges that form when a dense oceanic plate subducts under a less dense continental plate, melts in the mantle below, and then rises and bursts through the continental crust above.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first part is an independent clause, and what follows ("geological structures called arcs...") is a noun phrase that specifies the explanation. A colon correctly introduces it. C and D would leave a fragment; A runs the two together.

questions.passage: On March 23, 2021, a gust of wind wreaked havoc on global trade. Ever Given, an international shipping container vessel, became lodged in Egypt’s Suez Canal, a major shipping route between Europe and Asia. The vessel took six days to ______ it’s as heavy as two thousand blue whales when fully loaded.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: dislodge in part due to its sheer size,

options.label: B
options.text: dislodge, in part due to its sheer size:

options.label: C
options.text: dislodge, in part due to its sheer size,

options.label: D
options.text: dislodge, in part, due to its sheer size

questions.explanation: "In part due to its sheer size" is a supplementary phrase set off with a comma. The next part ("it’s as heavy as...") is an independent clause that explains the size, so a colon is appropriate. A and C create comma splices; D is a run-on.

questions.passage: Traditional Mandé drumming ensembles rely on three bass drums, known collectively as dunun, to anchor their polyrhythmic ______ the dununba, the sangban, and the kenkeni.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: An independent clause announces "three bass drums," and a list names them. A colon introduces a list after a complete clause. A semicolon (B) cannot introduce a list that isn't an independent clause.

questions.passage: Industrial chemists searching for a cost-effective alternative to platinum catalysts focused their research on a single abundant ______
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a single word that names or specifies what the clause announced ("a single abundant element"). A semicolon or period (B, C) would need an independent clause after it; D says the chemists studied two things, which is illogical.

sections.title: Colon Traps: No Colon After a Verb, “such as,” or “including”
sections.explanation_en: Because a colon needs a complete clause before it, it is illegal right after a verb (are, were, include), a preposition, or the words such as / including. These words already lead into the list, so they are followed by no punctuation at all. Fix a verb + colon by completing the clause first: ✘ "The goals were: …" → ✔ "The goals were threefold: …" or ✔ "The goals were to …"
sections.explanation_zh: 因為冒號前面必須是完整子句，所以冒號不可以直接放在動詞（are, were, include）、介系詞，或 such as / including 後面。這些字本身就會引出後面的清單，後面什麼標點都不加。如果是「動詞 + 冒號」的錯誤，要先把子句補完整：✘ The goals were: … → ✔ The goals were threefold: … 或 ✔ The goals were to …
examples: In assessing the films of Japanese director Akira Kurosawa, many critics have focused on Kurosawa’s use of Western literary sources but have missed his equally deep engagement with Japanese artistic traditions such as Noh theater. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q22 (no punctuation after “such as”)]

Formed in 1967 to foster political and economic stability within the Asia-Pacific region, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations was originally made up of five members: Thailand, the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q21 (complete clause before the colon)]

questions.passage: Among the primary advantages of early movable-type printing presses ______ rapid duplication of text, decreased production costs, and increased literacy across Europe.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject is the list ("rapid duplication..., decreased costs, and increased literacy") and the verb is "were." No punctuation may separate a verb from its subject/complement. A colon needs a complete clause before it—"Among the advantages were" is not complete.

questions.passage: The urban wetland restoration project aimed to preserve habitat for vulnerable bird species such ______ the blue heron, the snowy egret, and the belted kingfisher.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Such as" already introduces the examples; it is never followed by a colon, semicolon, or comma. A colon also requires a complete clause before it.

questions.passage: The three finalists in this year’s international robotics competition ______ teams from Seoul, Nairobi, and Monterrey.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The three finalists…were" is not a complete clause until the verb has its complement, so no colon (or any punctuation) may separate "were" from "teams from Seoul, Nairobi, and Monterrey."

questions.passage: The museum’s new Asian art wing displays artifacts ______ jade carvings, bronze vessels, and silk scrolls from the Song dynasty.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Including" (like "such as") already introduces the examples, so no punctuation follows it.

questions.passage: The bakery’s famous sourdough bread requires only three ______ flour, water, and salt.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The bakery's famous sourdough bread requires only three ingredients" is a complete clause that announces a list, so a colon is correct. B uses a semicolon before a list; C puts a colon after "such as"; D creates a second verb with no subject.

sections.title: Commas After Introductory Elements and Dependent Clauses
sections.explanation_en: A dependent clause starts with a word like because, although, while, when, if, since, whenever. It cannot stand alone. When it comes first, put a comma after it before the main clause. When a while/whereas contrast clause comes second, use a comma before it. An essential clause that tells when/under what condition at the end of the sentence usually takes no comma ("…is added whenever…"). Introductory phrases (participial, prepositional, infinitive) are also followed by a comma—after the whole phrase, never inside it. A dependent clause can never be separated from its main clause by a period, semicolon, or dash.
sections.explanation_zh: 從屬子句以 because, although, while, when, if, since, whenever 等字開頭，不能單獨成句。從屬子句放在句首時，後面加逗號再接主要子句。表示對比的 while / whereas 子句放在後面時，前面加逗號。放在句尾、說明「何時／在什麼條件下」的必要子句通常不加逗號（…is added whenever…）。開頭的片語（分詞片語、介系詞片語、不定詞片語）後面也要加逗號——加在整個片語之後，不要加在片語中間。從屬子句和主要子句之間絕對不能用句號、分號或破折號分開。
examples: When they were first introduced to western Europe from Byzantium in the eleventh century, table forks were met with much resistance. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q20]

Featuring jagged peaks of black ink surrounded by hazy swirls of blue and green paint, Zhang Daqian’s 1983 painting Panorama of Mount Lu is inspired by the tradition of qinglü shanshui, a type of Chinese landscape painting characterized by the use of blue and green hues to depict ethereal, otherworldly landscapes. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q23]

questions.passage: Although sauropod dinosaurs possessed air-filled bones that reduced overall skeletal ______ their massive body weight still required column-like limbs for support.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Although..." makes the first part a dependent clause. A dependent clause joins the main clause with a comma. A semicolon or period (A, C) would leave the "Although" clause as a fragment.

questions.passage: Because synthetic RNA guides can target specific DNA sequences with unprecedented ______ bioengineers can disable defective genes without disrupting surrounding cellular structures.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Because..." is a dependent clause; it attaches to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon or period leaves a fragment, and a single dash may follow only an independent clause.

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q19 — also SAT 10 M1 Q23
questions.passage: While many video game creators strive to make their graphics ever more ______ others look to the past, developing titles with visuals inspired by the “8-bit” games of the 1980s and 1990s. (The term “8-bit” refers to a console whose processor could only handle eight bits of data at once.)
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "While…lifelike" is an introductory dependent clause, so a comma separates it from the main clause "others look to the past." Adding "but" (A, D) is wrong because "while" already links the clauses; B lacks the needed comma.

questions.passage: The life spans of rockfish vary greatly by species. For instance, the colorful calico rockfish (Sebastes dalli) can survive for a little over a ______ the rougheye rockfish (Sebastes aleutianus) boasts a maximum life span of about two centuries.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "While the rougheye rockfish boasts..." is a dependent clause showing contrast, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. A period or semicolon (B, C) would leave it as a fragment; a colon (A) is not used before a dependent clause here.

questions.passage: The Lion Light system, developed by Kenyan inventor Richard Turere, consists of LED lights installed around the perimeter of livestock pastures. Powered with ______ the blinking LEDs keep lions away at night, thus protecting the livestock without risking harm to the endangered lions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: energy collected, by solar panels, during the day

options.label: B
options.text: energy collected by solar panels during the day

options.label: C
options.text: energy collected by solar panels during the day,

options.label: D
options.text: energy, collected by solar panels during the day,

questions.explanation: The introductory phrase "Powered with energy collected by solar panels during the day" must be followed by a comma before the main clause. Its internal parts are essential, so no internal commas are needed.

sections.title: Essential Appositives: Title + Name Takes No Commas
sections.explanation_en: An appositive is a noun that renames another noun. When a title or description comes directly before a name ("plant cell biologist Yuree Lee," "portrait artist Marie-Denise Villers," "the chemical compound aluminum oxide"), the name is essential—it tells us which person or thing—so no commas are used. Also remember that no comma may separate the whole subject from its verb.
sections.explanation_zh: 同位語是用來重新說明另一個名詞的名詞。當頭銜或描述直接放在名字前面時（plant cell biologist Yuree Lee、portrait artist Marie-Denise Villers、the chemical compound aluminum oxide），這個名字是必要的，告訴我們「是哪一位／哪一個」，所以不加逗號。另外也要記得：整個主詞和它的動詞之間不能加逗號。
examples: When writing The Other Black Girl (2021), novelist Zakiya Dalila Harris drew on her own experiences working at a publishing office. [Digital SAT 1, Module 2, Q19]
Brazilian biologist Mariana Nery believes the answer might be found in whales’ DNA. [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q18]

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q23 — also SAT 1 M2 Q27
questions.passage: Stomata, tiny pore structures in a leaf that absorb gases needed for plant growth, open when guard cells surrounding each pore swell with water. In a pivotal 2007 article, plant cell ______ showed that lipid molecules called phosphatidylinositol phosphates are responsible for signaling guard cells to open stomata.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Plant cell biologist Yuree Lee" is a title + name (restrictive), so no commas. No punctuation belongs between the subject and the verb "showed."

questions.passage: Long attributed to Jacques-Louis David, the preeminent Neoclassical painter of his day, the 1801 painting Marie Joséphine Charlotte du Val d’Ognes gained fresh attention in the 1990s when art historians discovered that the painting—which depicts a solitary young woman sketching—was actually the work of little-known French portrait ______ Marie-Denise Villers (1774–1821).
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Marie-Denise Villers" is an essential (restrictive) appositive identifying which portrait artist, so no punctuation separates it from "artist."

questions.passage: Paintings by the renowned twentieth-century US ______ were featured in Artist to Artist, an exhibition at the Smithsonian Art Museum that paired the works of artists whose career trajectories intersected in meaningful ways.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: artists: Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock,

options.label: B
options.text: artists Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock

options.label: C
options.text: artists Thomas Hart Benton, and Jackson Pollock,

options.label: D
options.text: artists, Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock

questions.explanation: The names are a restrictive appositive identifying which artists, so no punctuation is used. Also, no punctuation belongs between the subject and the verb "were featured."

questions.passage: In 1937, Chinese American screen actor Anna May Wong, who had portrayed numerous villains and secondary characters but never a heroine, finally got a starring role in Paramount Pictures’ Daughter of Shanghai, a film that ______ “expanded the range of possibilities for Asian images on screen.”
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Critic Stina Chyn" is a title + name (restrictive appositive), so no commas around the name. No comma belongs between the subject and the verb "claims" or between "claims" and the quotation that serves as its content.

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q27 — also SAT 9 M2 Q24
questions.passage: When external forces are applied to common glass made from silicates, energy builds up around minuscule defects in the material, resulting in fractures. Recently, engineer Erkka Frankberg of Tampere University in Finland used the chemical ______ to make a glassy solid that can withstand higher strain than silicate glass can before fracturing.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Aluminum oxide" is an essential (restrictive) appositive identifying which compound; it takes no commas. Nothing should separate the object from "to make."

sections.title: Other Essential Elements: “that” Clauses, Titles of Works, Essential Phrases
sections.explanation_en: Any word group that identifies which one is essential and takes no commas: a that-clause ("a company that specializes in…"), the title of a work after a common noun ("her 2019 novel Gingerbread offers…"), an essential participial phrase ("Students enrolled in the course must…"), or an essential time clause at the end of a sentence ("…is added whenever…"). Adding commas would either split the subject from its verb or change the meaning.
sections.explanation_zh: 凡是用來指明「是哪一個」的字組都是必要成分，不加逗號：that 子句（a company that specializes in…）、普通名詞後面的作品名稱（her 2019 novel Gingerbread offers…）、必要的分詞片語（Students enrolled in the course must…），以及放在句尾的必要時間子句（…is added whenever…）。如果加上逗號，會把主詞和動詞切開，或改變句子的意思。
examples: Former First Lady of the United States Eleanor Roosevelt and Indian activist and educator Hansa Mehta were instrumental in drafting the United Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a document that outlines the basic freedoms to which all people are entitled. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q20]

Researchers studying the “terra-cotta army,” the thousands of life-size statues of warriors found interred near the tomb of Emperor Qin Shi Huang of China, were shocked to realize that the shape of each statue’s ears, like the shape of each person’s ears, is unique. [Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q26]

questions.passage: Both Sona Charaipotra, an Indian American, and Dhonielle Clayton, an African American, grew up frustrated by the lack of diverse characters in books for young people. In 2011, these two writers joined forces to found CAKE Literary, a book packaging ______ specializes in the creation and promotion of stories told from diverse perspectives for children and young adults.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "That specializes in..." is an essential relative clause describing the company; it needs the relative pronoun "that" and no comma. A and C lack a connecting word; D wrongly uses a comma before "that."

questions.passage: As British scientist Peter Whibberley has observed, “the Earth is not a very good timekeeper.” Earth’s slightly irregular rotation rate means that measurements of time must be periodically adjusted. Specifically, an extra “leap second” (the 86,401st second of the day) is ______ time based on the planet’s rotation lags a full nine-tenths of a second behind time kept by precise atomic clocks.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Whenever time...lags" is an essential dependent clause telling when the second is added, so no punctuation is needed. B and C would leave the dependent clause as a fragment; A inserts an unnecessary comma.

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q28 — also SAT 9 M2 Q22
questions.passage: In crafting her fantasy fiction, Nigerian-born British author Helen Oyeyemi has drawn inspiration from the classic nineteenth-century fairy tales of the Brothers Grimm. Her 2014 novel Boy, Snow, Bird, for instance, is a complex retelling of the story of Snow White, while her 2019 novel ______ offers a delicious twist on the classic tale of Hansel and Gretel.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Her 2019 novel Gingerbread" is the subject of the clause and "offers" is its verb. No punctuation should separate a subject from its verb, and the title is an essential (restrictive) identifier.

questions.passage: Fans of the film Moana (2016) may not know that the deep and humorous voice behind the ______ belongs to comedian, actor, and musician Jemaine Clement. The versatile performer has appeared in everything from television commercials to action movies, but voice acting, specifically, has become a notable part of his career.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Tamatoa the crab" is a restrictive appositive identifying which character, so no commas are used. Also, no punctuation belongs between the subject ("the...voice behind the character Tamatoa the crab") and the verb "belongs."

questions.passage: Students ______ the advanced literature course must complete a summer reading assignment before the first class.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Enrolled in the advanced literature course" tells WHICH students (essential), so no commas. With commas (C) the sentence would say that all students are enrolled; A separates the subject from its verb.

sections.title: Nonessential Elements: Paired Commas
sections.explanation_en: A nonessential element adds extra information; if you delete it, the sentence is still complete and still means the same thing. It must be set off by matching punctuation on both sides—usually a pair of commas. Most SAT questions give you the opening comma earlier in the sentence and ask you to supply the closing one. Deletion test: remove the words between the commas—the remaining sentence must be grammatical.
sections.explanation_zh: 非必要成分是額外補充的資訊；刪掉它，句子仍然完整，意思也不變。它的前後必須用相同的標點隔開，最常見的是一對逗號。SAT 題目常常在前面已經給了開頭的逗號，要你補上結尾的逗號。刪除測試：把兩個逗號之間的字刪掉，剩下的句子必須合乎文法。
examples: Bengali author Toru Dutt’s A Sheaf Gleaned in French Fields (1876), a volume of English translations of French poems, has enhanced scholars’ understanding of the transnational and multilingual contexts in which Dutt lived and worked. [Digital SAT 3, Module 1, Q24]

In 2016, engineer Vanessa Galvez oversaw the installation of 164 bioswales, vegetated channels designed to absorb and divert stormwater, along the streets of Queens, New York. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q25]

questions.passage: Linguists studying ancient Sumerian cuneiform tablets, ______ have discovered that sentence syntax rules shifted rapidly during the Early Dynastic Period.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: many of whom were previously skeptical

options.label: B
options.text: many of whom were previously skeptical,

options.label: C
options.text: many of whom were previously skeptical;

options.label: D
options.text: many of whom, were previously skeptical

questions.explanation: The comma after "tablets" opens a nonessential relative clause ("many of whom were previously skeptical"). It must be closed with a matching comma before the main verb "have discovered."

questions.passage: Julia Alvarez’s 1994 novel In the Time of the Butterflies, a fictionalized account of the lives of the Mirabal ______ can serve as a starting point for those wanting to explore how the rule of dictator Rafael Trujillo has been represented in Dominican American literature.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The appositive "a fictionalized account...Mirabal sisters" is opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb "can serve." Adding "and" would create a compound subject with no verb logic.

questions.passage: English poet and Shakespeare contemporary John Donne’s ______ much admired during his lifetime (1572–1631) and in the decades that followed, had, at the time of their enthusiastic rediscovery by the early twentieth-century modernists, been essentially gathering dust for the intervening 250 years.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The main verb is "had...been gathering." "Much admired during his lifetime..." is a nonessential participial phrase that must be set off by commas; it needs an opening comma after "works." Adding "were" or "had been" creates two main verbs.

questions.passage: A study led by scientist Rebecca Kirby at the University of Wisconsin–Madison found that black bears that eat human food before hibernation have increased levels of a rare carbon isotope, ______ due to the higher 13C levels in corn and cane sugar. Bears with these elevated levels were also found to have much shorter hibernation periods on average.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Carbon-13 (13C)" is a nonessential appositive opened by the comma after "isotope," so it must close with a comma. The parenthetical abbreviation stays attached to "carbon-13" with no comma in between.

questions.passage: Langston Hughes's poetry collection The Weary Blues, published in 1926 during the height of the Harlem ______ fused traditional verse structures with blues rhythms.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The comma after the title opens a nonessential participial phrase; it must close with the matching mark—another comma—before the verb "fused." A mixes a comma with a dash.

sections.title: Nonessential Elements: Paired Dashes
sections.explanation_en: Paired dashes work exactly like paired commas but give more emphasis. The key rule: whatever mark opens the interrupter must close it. If it opens with a dash, it must close with a dash—never mix a dash with a comma. Always scan left in the sentence to see whether a dash has already opened an interrupter.
sections.explanation_zh: 一對破折號的功能和一對逗號完全相同，只是語氣更強調。關鍵規則：插入語用什麼標點開始，就要用同樣的標點結束。以破折號開始，就必須以破折號結束——絕對不可以破折號配逗號。一定要往左看，確認句子前面是否已經用破折號開啟了插入語。
examples: Earth’s auroras—colorful displays of light seen above the northern and southern poles—result, broadly speaking, from the Sun’s activity. [Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q28]

Working from an earlier discovery of Charpentier’s, chemists Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna—winners of the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry—re-created and then reprogrammed the so-called “genetic scissors” of a species of DNA-cleaving bacteria to forge a tool that is revolutionizing the field of gene technology. [Digital SAT 4, Module 2, Q24]

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q24 — also SAT 8 M2 Q23
questions.passage: The forty-seven geothermal springs of Arkansas’ Hot Springs National Park are sourced via a process known as natural groundwater recharge, in which rainwater percolates downward through the earth—in this case, the porous rocks of the hills around Hot ______ collect in a subterranean basin.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The supplementary phrase "in this case, the porous rocks...Hot Springs" opens with a dash, so it must close with a matching dash before the sentence resumes ("percolates downward through the earth...to collect").

questions.passage: In 1986, conceptual artist Sophie Calle asked twenty-three people, all of whom had been born without sight, to describe “their image of beauty” in rich detail. Calle paired excerpts of these conversations with photographs—both of interviewees and the items they ______ to powerful effect in her exhibition The Blind.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: described, from hair to grass to sculptures

options.label: B
options.text: described, from hair to grass to sculptures—

options.label: C
options.text: described—from hair to grass to sculptures,

options.label: D
options.text: described: from hair to grass to sculptures

questions.explanation: The supplementary element begins with a dash after "photographs," so it must close with a dash before "to powerful effect." Inside it, a comma sets off the examples "from hair to grass to sculptures."

questions.passage: Neural pathways governing motor-skill acquisition—once believed to solidify permanently during early ______ remain remarkably adaptable throughout adulthood.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The interrupter opened with a dash after "acquisition," so it must close with a dash before the verb "remain." Never mix a dash with a comma (B).

questions.passage: The Great Barrier ______ the largest living structure on Earth—is visible from space.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The interrupter "arguably the largest living structure on Earth" closes with a dash, so it must also open with a dash. B mixes a comma with a dash.

questions.passage: Three spices—cumin, coriander, and ______ form the base of many South Asian curries.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The list is an interrupter that opened with a dash after "spices," so it must close with a dash before the verb "form."

sections.title: Participial Phrases (分詞構句) at the End of a Sentence, Including “thus / thereby + -ing”
sections.explanation_en: A participial phrase begins with an -ing or -ed verb and has no subject and no main verb, so it can never stand alone. When it comes after a complete clause to describe a result or add information, attach it with a comma—never a semicolon or period. The same rule applies to thus / thereby + -ing ("…, thus protecting the livestock"; "…, thereby leading to his demise"). Also: commas and periods go inside closing quotation marks.
sections.explanation_zh: 分詞片語以 -ing 或 -ed 動詞開頭，沒有主詞，也沒有主要動詞，所以不能單獨成句。它放在完整子句後面、用來說明結果或補充資訊時，要用逗號連接——絕不能用分號或句號。thus / thereby + V-ing 也一樣（…, thus protecting the livestock；…, thereby leading to his demise）。另外，逗號和句號要放在結尾引號的裡面。
examples: Upon recovering two years later, Henry resumed his reign, forcing an angered Richard from the royal court and precipitating a series of battles later known as the Wars of the Roses. [Digital SAT 1, Module 1, Q28]

A firefly uses specialized muscles to draw oxygen into its lower abdomen through narrow tubes, triggering a chemical reaction whereby the oxygen combines with chemicals in the firefly’s abdomen to produce a glow. [Digital SAT 9, Module 1, Q30]

questions.passage: Beatrix Potter is perhaps best known for writing and illustrating children’s books such as The Tale of Peter Rabbit (1902), but she also dedicated herself to mycology, the study of ______ more than 350 paintings of the fungal species she observed in nature and submitting her research on spore germination to the Linnean Society of London.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Producing...and submitting..." is a participial phrase describing how Potter dedicated herself, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon (A) or period (B) would leave the phrase as an incomplete sentence; C makes it seem the fungi are producing paintings.

questions.passage: In ancient Greece, an Epicurean was a follower of Epicurus, a philosopher whose beliefs revolved around the pursuit of pleasure. Epicurus defined pleasure as “the absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the ______ that all life’s virtues derived from this absence.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Positing that all life’s virtues derived..." is a participial phrase (no subject, no finite verb) describing Epicurus, so it attaches to the main clause with a comma, placed inside the closing quotation mark. A semicolon or period (C, D) would leave the phrase as a fragment; a colon (B) is not used before a participial phrase.

questions.passage: Merchants traversing the Pamir Mountains during the Han Dynasty exchanged woven silk and lapis lazuli for Central Asian ______ significantly altering the economic trajectory of regional trade networks.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Significantly altering..." is a participial phrase (no subject, no finite verb) describing a result of the main clause. It attaches with a comma. A semicolon or colon (C, D) would need an independent clause after it; A runs the phrase into "horses."

questions.passage: Engineers added a second spillway to the ______ the risk of overflow during spring floods.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Thus reducing the risk…" is a participial phrase showing a result, not an independent clause, so it attaches with a comma. A and C leave the phrase as a fragment; D adds an unnecessary comma.

questions.passage: The city replaced its entire fleet of diesel buses with electric ______ its transportation emissions by nearly forty percent.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Thereby cutting…" is a result phrase: comma before "thereby," then the -ing participle. B leaves a fragment; C uses a verb with no subject; D misplaces the comma.

sections.title: Absolute Phrases and Appositives at the End of a Sentence
sections.explanation_en: Two more phrase types attach to a complete clause with a comma. An absolute phrase is a noun + participle with no main verb ("…to be quilts, the stitching barely visible…"). An appositive at the end of a sentence is a noun phrase that renames the noun right before it ("…the “tragedy of the commons,” the view that…"); a summative appositive such as a finding that… renames the whole idea before it. Because neither is an independent clause, a semicolon or period before it is always wrong. A single dash may also be used for emphasis.
sections.explanation_zh: 還有兩種片語用逗號接在完整子句後面。獨立分詞構句（絕對片語）是「名詞 + 分詞」，沒有主要動詞（…to be quilts, the stitching barely visible…）。句尾同位語是用來重新說明前一個名詞的名詞片語（…“tragedy of the commons,” the view that…）；a finding that… 這類總結式同位語則是重新概括前面整件事。這兩種都不是獨立子句，所以前面用分號或句號一定是錯的。也可以用一個破折號來加強語氣。
examples: Known as the Brass Era, this period in automotive design is remembered for its grandeur and artistry, its vehicles highly prized by collectors for their ornate detailing and gleaming brass fittings. [Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q25 (absolute phrase)]

As such, Ostrom’s work is a repudiation of the “tragedy of the commons,” the view that individuals will inevitably overexploit a finite shared resource if given unfettered access to it. [Digital SAT 8, Module 2, Q31 (appositive at the end)]

questions.passage: From afar, African American fiber artist Bisa Butler’s portraits look like paintings, their depictions of human faces, bodies, and clothing so intricate that it seems only a fine brush could have rendered them. When viewed up close, however, the portraits reveal themselves to be ______ stitching barely visible among the thousands of pieces of printed, microcut fabric.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The stitching barely visible..." is an absolute phrase (no finite verb), so it attaches to the main clause with a comma. A, C, and D treat it as an independent clause, which it is not.

questions.passage: Recently unearthed Neronian tools in France dating to 54,000 years ago and attributed to Homo sapiens may provide evidence that interactions between Neanderthals and modern humans occurred 10,000 years earlier than was previously ______ finding that, if true, would overturn current theories about H. sapiens migration during the Upper Paleolithic.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A finding that..." is a noun phrase (appositive) summing up the preceding clause, not an independent clause, so it is attached with a comma. A and B would leave it as a fragment; C omits needed punctuation.

questions.passage: In her analysis of Edith Wharton’s The House of Mirth (1905), scholar Candace Waid observes that the novel depicts the upper classes of New York society as “consumed by the appetite of a soulless ______ an apt assessment given that The House of Mirth is set during the Gilded Age, a period marked by rapid industrialization, economic greed, and widening wealth disparities.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "An apt assessment..." is a noun phrase that renames/comments on the preceding clause, so it is set off with a comma. In American style, the comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. A and B wrongly add "and" to a phrase that isn't a clause; D has no punctuation.

questions.passage: The marathon runner crossed the finish ______ raised in triumph above her head.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Her arms raised in triumph" is an absolute phrase (noun + participle, no finite verb), so it attaches with a comma. B and C would leave it as a fragment.

questions.passage: Deep-field images captured by space telescopes revealed galaxies forming merely 300 million years after the Big ______ discovery that challenged prevailing cosmological models.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A discovery that challenged..." is a noun phrase that sums up the clause. A single dash (or a comma) attaches it. A semicolon or period (B, C) would require an independent clause; D runs the phrase in with no break.

sections.title: The Single Dash
sections.explanation_en: A single dash acts like a colon (or an emphatic comma) at the end of a sentence. It must follow a complete independent clause, and it introduces an explanation, a list, an example, or a summarizing phrase. A single dash can never follow a dependent clause. If a dash was already used earlier in the sentence to open an interrupter, the next dash must close it.
sections.explanation_zh: 單一破折號在句尾的作用就像冒號（或語氣較強的逗號）。它前面必須是完整的獨立子句，後面用來引出解釋、清單、例子或總結的片語。單一破折號絕不能放在從屬子句後面。如果句子前面已經用破折號開啟了插入語，下一個破折號就必須用來結束它。
examples: In this state, embryonic development is paused for as long as two years—longer than the life span of an adult killifish. [Digital SAT 2, Module 1, Q20]
At the age of twelve, she entered a contest to have a story published in American Girl magazine—and won. [Digital SAT 8, Module 1, Q19]

questions.passage: Reintroducing apex predators can trigger ripple effects across an entire ______ gray wolves, sea otters, and raptors all regulate herbivore populations and foster plant diversity.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A single dash works like a colon: after a complete clause, it introduces an explanation or example. B is a comma splice; C is a run-on.

questions.passage: After months of testing, the engineers finally identified the source of the ______ single loose wire in the control panel.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: After a complete clause, a single dash introduces a phrase that explains or specifies (here, what the source was). A semicolon or period (B, C) would need an independent clause after it.

questions.passage: Because the storm had knocked out power across the ______ students finished their final exams by candlelight.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Because the storm had knocked out power…" is a dependent clause. It attaches to the main clause with a comma. A single dash, semicolon, or period can follow only an independent clause.

questions.passage: For her solo hike across the desert, the explorer packed only what she truly ______ water, a compass, and a detailed map.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause is complete, and what follows is a list that specifies what she needed. A single dash (like a colon) introduces it. A semicolon cannot introduce a list; C and D run the clause into the list.

questions.passage: The space telescope revealed something no astronomer had ______ appeared to orbit two stars at the same time.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A single dash after the complete clause introduces the noun phrase that specifies the "something." B and C leave "a planet that appeared…" as a fragment; D inserts an incorrect comma before the essential clause "that appeared…"

sections.title: Where Punctuation Is Illegal: Subject–Verb, Verb–Object, Preposition–Object
sections.explanation_en: Many SAT answers are no punctuation. Never put a single comma, colon, semicolon, or dash between a subject and its verb, between a verb and its object, or between a preposition and its object. The SAT makes subjects very long ("The strings inside the instrument") so that the blank falls right before the verb. Find the verb: if the blank sits between the full subject and that verb, choose no punctuation—unless you are closing a pair of commas or dashes opened earlier.
sections.explanation_zh: 很多 SAT 題目的正確答案是不加標點。絕對不可以在主詞和動詞之間、動詞和受詞之間，或介系詞和受詞之間加上單一的逗號、冒號、分號或破折號。SAT 常把主詞寫得很長（The strings inside the instrument），讓空格剛好落在動詞前面。先找出動詞：如果空格位於完整主詞和動詞之間，就選不加標點——除非你是在結束前面已經開啟的一對逗號或破折號。
examples: The Progressive Era in the United States witnessed the rise of numerous Black women’s clubs, local organizations that advocated for racial and gender equality. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q24]

In the historical novel The Surrender Tree, Cuban American author Margarita Engle uses poetry rather than prose to tell the true story of Cuban folk hero Rosa La Bayamesa. [Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q20]

questions.passage: A harpsichord may look just like a piano, but the difference between the two instruments is easy to hear. When a harpsichord’s keys are pressed, the strings inside the ______ are plucked, not struck.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The strings inside the instrument" is the subject and "are plucked" is the verb. No punctuation belongs between a subject and its verb.

questions.passage: Nigerian American artist Toyin Ojih Odutola uses black-ink pens to create highly detailed drawings of human figures. Her portrait of novelist Zadie ______ is displayed in the National Portrait Gallery in London.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Her portrait of novelist Zadie Smith" is the subject, and "is displayed" is its verb. No punctuation belongs between a subject and its verb.

questions.passage: Louise Bennett (1919–2006), also known as “Miss Lou,” was an influential Jamaican poet and folklorist. Her innovative poems ______ the use of Jamaican Creole (a spoken language) in literature.
