questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "The use of Jamaican Creole" is the direct object of "popularized." No punctuation belongs between a verb and its object.

questions.passage: In her two major series “Memory Test” and “Autobiography,” painter Howardena Pindell explored themes ______ healing, self-discovery, and memory by cutting and sewing back together pieces of canvas and inserting personal artifacts, such as postcards, into some of the paintings.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: No punctuation belongs between a preposition ("of") and its object ("healing, self-discovery, and memory").

questions.passage: The dinosaur nests discovered in the Gobi Desert by the joint Mongolian-American research ______ that some species laid their eggs in large colonies.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The long subject is "The dinosaur nests discovered…by the joint Mongolian-American research team," and "reveal" is its verb. No punctuation may separate a subject from its verb.

sections.title: Semicolons + Commas in a Complex Series (Three Ideas)
sections.explanation_en: List items are normally separated by commas. But when the items already contain commas (a name + description, a city + country, a title + appositive), separate the items with semicolons so the reader can see where each item ends: item 1, detail; item 2, detail; and item 3, detail. Look ahead for "; and" before the last item—it tells you the list uses semicolons. The semicolon goes at the end of each item, never inside it.
sections.explanation_zh: 清單中的項目通常用逗號分開。但當每個項目本身已經含有逗號時（人名 + 說明、城市 + 國家、作品名 + 同位語），項目之間要改用分號，讓讀者看清每一項在哪裡結束：項目一, 說明; 項目二, 說明; and 項目三, 說明. 先往後看最後一項前是否有「; and」，有的話就代表這個清單用分號。分號放在每個項目的結尾，不可放在項目中間。
examples: These include overseeing the Library of Congress’s collections, which boast more than 162 million items; managing the US Copyright Office, which registers copyright claims and advises Congress on copyright law; and appointing the US poet laureate. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q23]

Buchi Emecheta’s celebrated literary oeuvre includes The Joys of Motherhood, a novel about the changing roles of women in 1950s Lagos; A Kind of Marriage, a television play about the private struggles of a newlywed couple in Nigeria; and Head Above Water, her autobiography. [Digital SAT 2, Module 2, Q26]

questions.passage: Joshua Hinson, director of the language revitalization program of the Chickasaw Nation in Oklahoma, helped produce the world’s first Indigenous-language instructional app, Chickasaw ______ Chickasaw TV, in 2010; and a Rosetta Stone language course in Chickasaw, in 2015.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: Basic; in 2009, an online television network;

options.label: B
options.text: Basic; in 2009, an online television network,

options.label: C
options.text: Basic, in 2009; an online television network,

options.label: D
options.text: Basic, in 2009, an online television network,

questions.explanation: This is a list of three items that contain internal commas, so the items are separated by semicolons. Item 1 is "the...app, Chickasaw Basic, in 2009"; the semicolon comes after "2009," and item 2 begins "an online television network, Chickasaw TV, in 2010."

questions.passage: The Arctic-Alpine Botanic Garden in Norway and the Jardim Botânico of Rio de Janeiro in Brazil are two of many botanical gardens around the world dedicated to growing diverse plant ______ fostering scientific research; and educating the public about plant conservation.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: This is a series of three items separated by semicolons ("; and educating..."). Item 1 contains an internal comma ("species, both native and nonnative"), so it ends with a semicolon.

questions.passage: Using natural debris, such as dried ______ such as plastic bags; and more traditional art supplies, such as tree glue, Ghanaian artist Ed Franklin Gavua creates his striking Yiiiiikakaii African masks, which he hopes can help viewers rethink how waste is used in their communities.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The list items contain internal commas, so items are separated with semicolons ("...leaves; man-made trash, such as plastic bags; and..."). Within item 2, a comma precedes "such as."

questions.passage: The international preservation team included Dr. Kenzo Sato, an urban preservationist from Tokyo ______ Dr. Maria Alvarez, an architectural historian from Madrid ______ and Thomas Wright, a structural engineer from London.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Each list item already contains a comma (name, description). To keep the three items distinct, separate them with semicolons at both blanks.

questions.passage: The science fair’s top prizes went to Priya Nair, a ninth grader from ______ Marcus Lee, whose solar-powered water filter impressed the judges; and Elena Ruiz, a senior from Austin, Texas.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The items already contain commas (name, description), and the last item begins with "; and," so each item must end with a semicolon. The comma between the city and state stays inside the item: "Dayton, Ohio;".

sections.title: Apostrophes with Nouns: Plurals vs. Possessives
sections.explanation_en: (1) Simple plural = no apostrophe (stories, hands, antennas). (2) Singular possessive = 's (the screw's threads). (3) Regular plural possessive = s' (the rocks' migration). (4) Irregular plural possessive = 's (people's stories, children's museum). Two steps: first decide whether the noun is singular or plural (look for clues like a, one vs. 162, all five); then ask whether it owns the next noun ("the threads of the screw"). If it owns nothing, it takes no apostrophe.
sections.explanation_zh: (1) 一般複數：不加撇號（stories, hands, antennas）。(2) 單數所有格：加 's（the screw's threads）。(3) 規則複數所有格：加 s'（the rocks' migration）。(4) 不規則複數所有格：加 's（people's stories, children's museum）。兩個步驟：先判斷名詞是單數還是複數（看 a, one 或 162, all five 等線索）；再問它是否擁有後面的名詞（the threads of the screw）。如果沒有擁有任何東西，就不加撇號。
examples: Currently, archaeologists’ efforts are aided by drones that capture high-resolution aerial photographs of the lines. [Digital SAT 3, Module 2, Q28 (plural possessive + simple plurals)]
Additionally, they help regulate a plant’s water loss. [Digital SAT 7, Module 1, Q27 (singular possessive)]

questions.passage: Inventor John Friedman created a prototype of the first flexible straw by inserting a screw into a paper straw and, using dental floss, binding the straw tightly around the ______ When the floss and screw were removed, the resulting corrugations in the paper allowed the straw to bend easily over the edge of a glass.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: There is one screw ("a screw"), so the singular possessive "screw’s" is needed. The threads belong to the screw and are plural but do not possess anything, so "threads" takes no apostrophe.

questions.passage: In Death Valley National Park’s Racetrack Playa, a flat, dry lakebed, are 162 rocks—some weighing less than a pound but others almost 700 pounds—that move periodically from place to place, seemingly of their own volition. Racetrack-like trails in the ______ mysterious migration.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: There is one playa, so "playa’s" (singular possessive) is correct. The migration belongs to the 162 rocks, so the plural possessive "rocks’" is required.

questions.passage: Literary agents estimate that more than half of all nonfiction books credited to a celebrity or other public figure are in fact written by ghostwriters, professional authors who are paid to write other ______ but whose names never appear on book covers.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "People" is already plural, so its possessive is "people’s." "Stories" is a plural noun that owns nothing, so it takes no apostrophe.

questions.passage: In his groundbreaking book Bengali Harlem and the Lost Histories of South Asian America, Vivek Bald uses newspaper articles, census records, ships’ logs, and memoirs to tell the ______ who made New York City their home in the early twentieth century.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: story’s of the South Asian immigrants

options.label: B
options.text: story’s of the South Asian immigrants’

options.label: C
options.text: stories of the South Asian immigrants

options.label: D
options.text: stories’ of the South Asian immigrant’s

questions.explanation: Neither "stories" nor "immigrants" possesses anything here, so both are simple plurals without apostrophes.

questions.passage: What makes the theremin a unique musical instrument? You play it without touching it. When you place your ______ the pitch will shift as your hands move through the air.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Hands" and "antennas" are simple plurals that do not possess anything, so neither takes an apostrophe. (Note: the source prints the transition stem for this item, but it tests Standard English conventions.)

sections.title: Apostrophes with Pronouns: its / it's, their / they're / there
sections.explanation_en: Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe: its, their, whose, yours. A word with an apostrophe is a contraction: it's = it is/it has, they're = they are, who's = who is. There is a place or "there is/are." Test by expanding the contraction: if "it is" or "they are" makes sense, use the apostrophe form. Also match number: its for a singular noun (including collective nouns like committee), their for plural nouns.
sections.explanation_zh: 所有格代名詞永遠不加撇號：its, their, whose, yours。有撇號的字是縮寫：it's = it is / it has，they're = they are，who's = who is。there 表示地點或「there is / are」。判斷方法：把縮寫展開，如果 it is 或 they are 講得通，就用有撇號的形式。另外要注意單複數：單數名詞（包括 committee 這類集合名詞）用 its，複數名詞用 their。
examples: Like other amphibians, the wood frog (Rana sylvatica) is unable to generate its own heat, so during periods of subfreezing temperatures, it survives by producing large amounts of glucose, a sugar that helps prevent damaging ice from forming inside its cells. [Digital SAT 4, Module 1, Q20]

When, in 2017, Cambridge University students Lucy Moss and Toby Marlow decided they wanted to develop a musical together, one of their goals was for their female actor friends to have good parts to play. [Digital SAT 7, Module 2, Q30]

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 9, Module 2, Q19 — also SAT 1 M1 Q21
questions.passage: British scientists James Watson and Francis Crick won the Nobel Prize in part for their 1953 paper announcing the double helix structure of DNA, but it is misleading to say that Watson and Crick discovered the double helix. ______ findings were based on a famous X-ray image of DNA fibers, “Photo 51,” developed by X-ray crystallographer Rosalind Franklin and her graduate student Raymond Gosling.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A plural possessive determiner is needed to show the findings belong to Watson and Crick: "Their." "They’re" and "It’s" are contractions; "Its" is singular.

questions.passage: In Marisol’s 1968 sculpture Mi Mama y Yo, gone are the types of pop culture references that made the Parisian-born Venezuelan American artist a star at the height of the pop art movement. In ______ place is a far more personal subject: a sculptural depiction of the artist as a young girl with her mother.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The possessive refers to "the types of pop culture references" (plural), which are gone; the new subject takes their place. So the plural possessive "their" is correct. "It’s" and "they’re" are contractions.

questions.passage: The machine-learning algorithm adjusts ______ internal parameters during training to minimize errors, ensuring that ______ capable of making accurate real-time predictions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Blank 1 shows possession (the algorithm's parameters): its—no apostrophe. Blank 2 means "it is capable": the contraction it's. "Its'" is never correct.

questions.passage: After three hours of debate, the selection committee announced that ______ decision on the scholarship winners would be final.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The decision belongs to the committee (a singular collective noun), so the possessive "its" is needed. "It's" = it is; "they're" = they are; "there" is a place word.

questions.passage: Sea otters are among the few mammals that use tools; ______ able to crack open shellfish by pounding them against stones balanced on their chests.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The blank needs a subject + verb: "they are able." The contraction "they're" = they are. "Their" is possessive, "there" is a place word, and "its" is singular possessive.

sections.title: Question Marks: Direct vs. Indirect Questions
sections.explanation_en: A direct question uses question word order (helping verb before the subject: "how do they affect…") and ends with a question mark. It often stands alone and is followed by a new sentence. An indirect question is reported inside a statement after verbs like investigated, wondered, debated, wanted to understand; it uses statement word order ("how people perceive…") and ends with a period.
sections.explanation_zh: 直接問句使用疑問句語序（助動詞在主詞前面：how do they affect…），句尾用問號，通常單獨成句，後面接著另一個新句子。間接問句是放在陳述句裡、跟在 investigated, wondered, debated, wanted to understand 等動詞後面的問句，使用陳述句語序（how people perceive…），句尾用句號。
examples: How did whales, once no bigger than seals, evolve to become the largest animals on Earth? [Digital SAT 5, Module 2, Q18 (direct question)]
Neuroscientist Karen Konkoly wanted to determine whether individuals can understand and respond to questions during REM sleep. [Digital SAT 10, Module 2, Q27 (indirect question)]

questions.passage: In forecasting weather events, meteorologists sometimes discuss the role of atmospheric rivers. What are atmospheric rivers, and how ______ Part of the water cycle, atmospheric rivers are narrow channels of moisture moving through the atmosphere. In certain conditions, these “rivers” can release some of their moisture as precipitation.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: This is a direct question ("What are atmospheric rivers, and how..."), so it needs question word order ("do they affect") and a question mark.

questions.source: Official Digital SAT 10, Module 2, Q19 — also SAT 1 M2 Q22
questions.passage: Lucía Michel of the University of Chile observed that alkaline soils contain an insoluble form of iron that blueberry plants cannot absorb, thus inhibiting blueberry growth. If these plants were grown in alkaline soil alongside grasses that aid in iron solubilization, ______ Michel was determined to find out.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: This is a direct question that Michel wanted answered ("...could the blueberries thrive? Michel was determined to find out."). A direct question uses inverted word order and a question mark.

questions.passage: Researchers Amit Kumar and Nicholas Epley investigated how ______ In a series of experiments conducted in 2022, they found that people performing small acts of kindness underestimated the positive effect their actions had on others.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: do people perceive acts of kindness.

options.label: B
options.text: do people perceive acts of kindness?

questions.explanation: This is an indirect (embedded) question inside a statement, so it uses statement word order (subject + verb: "people perceive") and ends with a period, not a question mark.

questions.passage: Researchers wanted to understand ______ The team designed an experiment that offered bees identical sugar water in dishes of different colors.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.label: A
options.text: why do bees prefer blue flowers?

options.label: D
options.text: why do bees prefer blue flowers.

questions.explanation: The question is reported inside a statement ("Researchers wanted to understand why..."), so it is an indirect question: statement word order (bees prefer) and a period.

questions.passage: Linguists have long debated ______ Some argue that it began with gestures; others believe it began with song.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The question is reported inside a statement ("Linguists have long debated how…"), so it is an indirect question: statement word order (language originated) and a period.
